fields.title: Introducing SpacePress: TypeScript That Compiles Directly to WordPress
fields.excerpt: Write schemas, SQL tables, access rules, server actions, background jobs, and TSX pages in TypeScript — compiled with Rust into native PHP and WordPress plugins with zero Node.js in production.

record.body:
Today we are introducing **SpacePress** (`spacepress.dev`) — a full-stack TypeScript framework whose Rust and OXC compiler turns your application directly into native PHP, numbered SQL migrations, OpenAPI 3.1, a typed client, and standard WordPress plugins.

## Why compile TypeScript to WordPress?

Teams building content-heavy products, editorial sites, and storefronts face an awkward split: either adopt a modern TypeScript stack and rebuild editorial workflows, media libraries, permissions, comments, and commerce from scratch — or adopt WordPress and give up end-to-end type safety, clean migrations, and modern component authoring.

SpacePress bridges both worlds without running a Node.js server in production:

- **One TypeScript schema, two storage engines:** Use `collection()` for WordPress posts (with Gutenberg, drafts, revisions, staged versions, and comments) right alongside `table()` for relational SQL tables with automatic migrations and compound indexes.
- **Native PHP compilation:** Declarative access rules, field validation, transactional hooks, `action()` RPC endpoints, Action Scheduler `job()` queues, custom `route.ts` handlers, and file-based TSX pages all compile directly to PHP.
- **Progressive interactivity:** Forms bound to server actions work without JavaScript, while `"use client"` components compile to WordPress Interactivity API stores with `useState` and live-updating `useLive()`.
- **Ecosystem included:** Native WooCommerce store & optimistic cart hooks, React Email transactional templates, two-way Markdown & Git sync, modern SpacePress Admin (`/wp-admin/new/`), `@spacepress/blocks` for Gutenberg in TSX, `@spacepress/astro` for external frontends, and a built-in MCP server for AI coding agents.

## Built with SpacePress itself

Everything you are reading on **spacepress.dev** is itself a real SpacePress application:

- This blog post is synced from `www/content/posts/introducing-spacepress.md` via `wp.posts.extend()` and rendered through `sp/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` with WordPress's native `<Comments>` component.
- The `/docs` section is synced from `www/content/docs/**/*.md` into a hierarchical `docs` collection rendered with `nav()`, `pager()`, and `headings()`.
- The `/examples` directory lives in a custom SQL `table()` whose GitHub star counts refresh asynchronously on Action Scheduler via the `refreshStars` job.
- Saved links in the `/play` browser playground are stored in the `shares` SQL table via the `share` server action, while the live compiler sandboxes across `/`, `/quick-start`, `/guide`, and `/play` run our real Rust compiler compiled to WebAssembly (`compiler.wasm`).

## Try it now

Head to the [Quick Start](/quick-start) to launch a local WordPress site in under three minutes, explore the [Interactive Engineering Guide](/guide) with live compiler sandboxes in every section, or jump straight into the [Playground](/play) right in your browser.

fields.title: Pages, Layouts & Interactive Islands
fields.description: File-based TSX routing compiled to PHP, progressive forms, "use client" Interactivity API islands, and static export.

record.body:
## File-based routing in `sp/app/`

SpacePress compiles TSX pages and layouts in `sp/app/` directly into server-rendered PHP:

- `sp/app/layout.tsx` — shared shell, `export const template = "theme" | "blank" | "<slug>"`, `metadata`, and CSS imports.
- `sp/app/page.tsx`, `[slug]/page.tsx`, `[...path]/page.tsx`, `(group)/` — static, dynamic, catch-all, and grouped routes.
- `sp/app/not-found.tsx` and `sp/app/login.tsx` — custom 404 and custom WordPress sign-in screens.
- `export const search = { page: integer().default(1) }` — typed query string parsing.
- `export const guard = "authenticated"` — route-level authorization.

## Built-in server components (`spacepress/app`)

Use `<Link>` (Interactivity Router navigation), `<Content>` (block content via `the_content`), `<Html>` (sanitized HTML), `<Comments>`, `<Pagination>`, `<Search>`, `<SearchResults>`, `<LoginForm>`, `<TemplatePart>`, `<Live id="...">`, and `useFormState(action)` for progressive zero-JS `<form action={myAction}>` submissions.

## `"use client"` interactive islands (`spacepress/client`)

Start a component file with `"use client";`. SpacePress renders its initial HTML in PHP and compiles the interactive logic into a WordPress Interactivity API store supporting `useState`, `useEffect`, `useMount`, `useEvent`, `useRef`, `sharedState`, and live-updating `useLive(kind, query)` subscriptions.

## Static export

Set `output: "static"` in `defineConfig()` and export `staticParams()` on dynamic routes, then run `spacepress export` to emit a standalone static site to `sp/dist/static/`.

fields.title: Schema & Storage
fields.description: Collections, SQL tables, globals, WordPress built-in kinds, field builders, and migrations.

record.body:
## Choosing a storage kind

| Builder             | Storage                     | When to use                                                                                                    |
|---------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `collection()`      | WordPress custom post type  | Editorial items needing Gutenberg, drafts, revisions, staged versions, comments, URL routing, or Markdown sync |
| `table()`           | Dedicated SQL table         | Relational app records, high-volume data, compound indexes (`.index()`), strict SQL migrations                 |
| `global()`          | WordPress options singleton | Site-wide settings, navigation links, feature flags                                                            |
| `wp.posts.extend()` | Built-in WordPress `post`   | Native blog posts extended with typed meta fields and URL pattern                                              |
| `userProjection()`  | `wp_users` + `wp_usermeta`  | Typed user profiles without duplicating WordPress accounts                                                     |
| `taxonomy()`        | WordPress term tables       | Flat or hierarchical vocabularies attached via `on: [...]` or `terms()`                                        |

## Field builders

All columns are `NOT NULL` by default unless `.optional()` is chained.

- **Scalars:** `text({ multiline? })`, `integer()`, `number()`, `boolean()`, `date()`, `timestamp()`, `json<T>()`
- **Semantic:** `email()`, `url()`, `slug({ source })`, `richText()`, `select([...])` (`.many()` for multi-select)
- **Relations & Media:** `ref(kind)` (`.many()`, `.onDelete("cascade" | "restrict" | "setNull")`, `.reverse("name")`), `terms(taxonomy)`, `media({ accept })`, `file(bucket)`
- **Structured:** `group(fields)`, `repeater(fields)`, `blocks(layouts)`

## Modifiers & safe renames

Chain `.min(n)`, `.max(n)`, `.pattern(/.../)`, `.unique()`, `.default(v)`, `.defaultNow()`, `.$default(fn)`, `.$onUpdate(fn)`, `.validate((v, ctx) => ...)`, `.ui({ label, help, placeholder, width })`, and `.showIf({ ... })`.

To rename a column or SQL table without losing production data, declare `.was("oldName")` on the column or `was: "old_table"` on `table()`. SpacePress emits a safe rename migration against `sp/_generated/migrations/snapshot.json`.

fields.title: Installation & Setup
fields.description: Requirements, creating a new app, and starting the local WordPress development environment.

record.body:
## Requirements

- **Node.js 22 or newer** and npm
- No Docker and no Rust toolchain required — the `spacepress` npm package downloads a prebuilt native compiler binary automatically.

## Create a new application

```bash
npm create spacepress@0.3.0 my-app
cd my-app
npm run dev
```

`create-spacepress` creates a complete starter project with:

- `spacepress.config.ts` defining a synced `notes` collection and `site` global
- `sp/app/` with a layout, home page, dynamic `/notes/[slug]` page, and a progressive `<form action={greet}>`
- `content/notes/` sample Markdown content
- `AGENTS.md`, `.mcp.json`, and coding-agent skills generated via `spacepress init`

## Running locally

`npm run dev` invokes `spacepress dev`, which compiles your TypeScript, boots a local WordPress + SQLite server, activates the compiled plugins, and rebuilds automatically on file changes.

- Open the printed site URL to view your rendered TSX pages.
- Open `/wp-admin/new/` to explore SpacePress Admin (or `/wp-admin/` for classic wp-admin).
- Stop the dev server without deleting local data via `npm run stop` (`spacepress dev stop`).

## Adding modules

Add first-party modules as source files you own at any time:

```bash
npx spacepress add shop           # WooCommerce storefront & catalog
npx spacepress add db             # SQL table starter
npx spacepress add api-reference  # /api documentation pages from OpenAPI
```

fields.title: Project Structure
fields.description: Layout of a SpacePress repository, authored files vs generated artifacts.

record.body:
## Directory layout

```text
my-app/
├── spacepress.config.ts   # Entry point: defineConfig() + re-exports
├── tsconfig.json          # Maps "spacepress", "spacepress/*", "spacepress:db"
├── sp/
│   ├── schema.ts          # Collections, SQL tables, globals, taxonomies, stores
│   ├── server.ts          # Actions, background jobs, mail helpers
│   ├── app/               # File-based TSX pages, layouts, and route.ts handlers
│   ├── components/        # Server and "use client" components
│   ├── wp-hooks/          # Typed WordPress core action & filter handlers
│   ├── _generated/        # db.d.ts, routes.d.ts, openapi.json, client/, migrations/
│   └── dist/wp-content/   # Compiled WordPress plugins ready to deploy
├── content/               # Markdown/JSON content synced with WordPress
├── emails/                # React Email (.tsx) templates
└── public/                # Static assets served from site root
```

## What to commit to Git

Commit everything you author (`spacepress.config.ts`, `sp/schema.ts`, `sp/app/`, `content/`, `emails/`, `public/`) **plus** these compiler lock/ledger files:

- `sp/_generated/migrations/` (`snapshot.json` and numbered `*.sql` files) — tracks schema history for safe incremental deploys.
- `sp/_generated/wp-plugins.lock.json` — locks WordPress plugin versions and SHA-256 checksums.
- `sp/_generated/plugins.lock.json` — locks capability grants for `use` plugin packages.
- `sp/_generated/abilities.json` & `sp/_generated/runtime-schema.json` — when using pulled WordPress Abilities or runtime schema versions.

`sp/dist/` is a build artifact and is typically git-ignored.

fields.title: Astro & Generated Typed Clients
fields.description: Connect external React, Next.js, Vite, or Astro frontends to a SpacePress backend.

record.body:
## Generated TypeScript client & React hooks

Every build emits a typed client to `sp/_generated/client/`:

- `index.ts` — `createClient({ baseUrl })` for CRUD queries, pagination, live subscriptions, and typed server actions.
- `react.ts` — `createHooks(React)` returning `useQuery()` and `useMutation()` (with `optimistic` updates and rollback) for React 18+ or Preact without bundling React into SpacePress.

## `@spacepress/astro`

For Astro 7+ sites, install `@spacepress/astro`:

- `spLoader(kind, opts)` — build-time Astro Content Layer loader with relation and media expansion.
- `spLiveLoader(kind, opts)` — live on-demand loader returning `cacheHint.tags` (`<kind>`, `<kind>:<id>`).
- `spWebhook(opts)` — Astro API route handler verifying `SpacePress-Signature` HMAC headers and invalidating cache tags automatically.

Set `frontend: "https://your-astro-site.com"` in `defineConfig()` so WordPress permalinks, previews, and feeds point to your Astro deployment.

fields.title: Two-Way Markdown & Git Sync
fields.description: Synchronize Markdown/JSON files in Git with WordPress collections and taxonomies.

record.body:
## Configuring sync

Add a `sync` glob to any `collection()`, `wp.posts.extend()`, `taxonomy()`, `product()`, or `table()`:

```ts
export const docs = collection({
  title: text(),
  slug: slug({ source: "title" }),
  content: richText().optional(),
}, {
  hierarchical: true,
  url: "/docs/:path",
  sync: "content/docs/**/*.md",
});
```

A `**` folder pattern maps subdirectories into parent/child hierarchy (`index.md` represents the folder item). Every synced record receives an immutable `uid` so renames and slug changes stay linked.

## Running sync & CI workflows

- Run `spacepress sync` to perform a 3-way merge between local Markdown files and WordPress. Front matter is validated against your TypeScript schema before writing.
- Run `spacepress init --github` to scaffold GitHub Actions for automated content sync.
- Configure `spacepress git-dispatch` so edits saved inside WordPress Admin trigger a repository dispatch event automatically.
- Enable `seed: true` in `defineConfig()` to populate synced records when a fresh deployment activates the plugin without overwriting existing editorial changes.

fields.title: CLI & Deployment
fields.description: Build, check, export, push, doctor, plugin packaging, and production hosting options.

record.body:
## Core build & deploy commands

- `spacepress dev` / `dev stop` / `dev status` — manage the local WordPress + SQLite site.
- `spacepress check [--json] [--frozen]` — compile and report diagnostics without writing output.
- `spacepress build` — emit WordPress plugins into `sp/dist/wp-content/plugins/`, migrations, types, client, and OpenAPI.
- `spacepress export [--site <url>]` — prebuild `sp/app/` into `sp/dist/static/` (`output: "static"`).
- `spacepress plugin` — package an uploadable `spacepress.zip` plugin for `wp-admin`.
- `spacepress login <site-url>` & `spacepress push` — authenticate via WordPress Application Passwords and deploy directly to a remote WordPress site.
- `spacepress doctor [--links]` — verify build integrity, live site plugins, and crawl internal links/anchors.

## Site operations (WP-CLI bridge)

Target local dev (default) or any remote site (`--site <dir | workspace | @alias>`):

- `spacepress wp <args...>` — run any WP-CLI command.
- `spacepress migrate`, `seed`, `jobs`, `staged`, `publish-due`, `identity`, `find`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `action`, `abilities`, `run`.

## Hosting & deployment guides

SpacePress runs anywhere WordPress 7.1+ and PHP 8.2+ run:

- **[Deploy on Spacefast](/docs/operations/deploy-spacefast)**
- **[Deploy on Pressable](/docs/operations/deploy-pressable)**
- **[Deploy on WordPress.com](/docs/operations/deploy-wordpress-com)**
- **[Deploy on Self-hosted WordPress](/docs/operations/deploy-self-hosted)**

## Sealed mode & plugin lockfile

Declare third-party WordPress plugins in `defineConfig({ plugins: { ... }, sealed: true })`. Exact versions and SHA-256 checksums are locked in `sp/_generated/wp-plugins.lock.json`, and sealed mode refuses activation of undeclared plugins.

fields.title: MCP & AI Agents
fields.description: Project MCP server, AGENTS.md scaffolding, WordPress Abilities API, and runtime schema versions.

record.body:
## Coding agent setup

Run `spacepress init` in any project to write `AGENTS.md`, `.mcp.json`, and agent skills tailored to your schema and config. Run `spacepress init --check` in CI to ensure they stay up to date.

## Stdio MCP server

`spacepress mcp` launches a local MCP server on stdio exposing:

- Embedded documentation compiled into the exact binary version you are running
- Live project schema, routes, and compiler diagnostics

## WordPress Abilities API

Every collection, global, action, and job is registered as a WordPress Ability by default (`agents: false` opts out). Annotate actions with `readonly: true` or `destructive: true` to guide agent safety checks.

To invoke abilities provided by WordPress core or installed plugins with full TypeScript types:

```bash
npx spacepress abilities pull --site https://example.com
```

Then call `abilities.call("ability/name", input)` from `"php/wordpress"` inside any action, hook, or route.

fields.title: Deploy on Pressable
fields.description: Deploy a SpacePress app to Pressable (WP Cloud) using the SpacePress plugin, Application Passwords, and spacepress push.

record.body:
[Pressable](https://pressable.com) runs managed WordPress on WP Cloud with PHP 8.2+, WordPress 7.1+, `ZipArchive`, WP-CLI over SSH, and Application Passwords enabled over HTTPS. `spacepress.dev` itself runs on Pressable.

## Prerequisites

- A Pressable site running **WordPress 7.1+** and **PHP 8.2+**
- Administrator access in `wp-admin` (or SSH/WP-CLI access)

## 1. Package and install the SpacePress plugin

Generate the uploadable host plugin (`spacepress.zip`):

```bash
npx spacepress plugin --out spacepress.zip
```

Install and activate `spacepress.zip` in **wp-admin → Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin**, or over SSH with WP-CLI:

```bash
wp plugin install spacepress.zip --activate --force
```

Activating the plugin automatically installs and activates its pinned platform dependencies (`action-scheduler`, `secure-custom-fields`, `two-factor`, `mcp-adapter`).

## 2. Sign in and push your build

Authenticate against your Pressable site and preview the deployment plan:

```bash
npx spacepress login https://your-site.example
npx spacepress push --dry-run
```

When the plan looks right, make it live:

```bash
npx spacepress push
```

In CI or non-interactive scripts, create a WordPress Application Password (`wp user application-password create <user> deploy --porcelain`) and pass `SP_APP_PASSWORD="<user>:<password>"`.

## 3. Sync Markdown content

If you use `sync: "content/**/*.md"`, push or pull Markdown edits after deploying:

```bash
npx spacepress sync --site https://your-site.example
```

## Pressable / WP Cloud hosting notes

- **Build store location:** On Pressable, PHP-FPM runs inside `/srv/htdocs` and cannot write outside it, so SpacePress automatically creates a randomized build store directory (`wp-content/spacepress-store-<random-hex>`). Keep that path private and never link to it publicly.
- **Root static files (`.js`, `.wasm`, `.txt`):** Pressable's nginx serves top-level static file extensions directly from `/srv/htdocs/` before reaching PHP. If your app ships custom scripts or WebAssembly assets under `public/` (like `public/site.js` or `public/compiler.wasm`), copy them into `/srv/htdocs/` during release so nginx serves them directly from the edge CDN.
- **Avoid `/files/` for public assets:** WP Cloud reserves `/files/*` for legacy WordPress Multisite rewrites. Place downloadable assets in another path (for example, `public/downloads/` or `public/playground-plugins/`).

fields.title: Deploy on Self-hosted WordPress
fields.description: Run SpacePress on your own VPS, Docker stack, or any LAMP/LEMP host with zero lock-in — via spacepress push or standalone plugins.

record.body:
Because SpacePress compiles into standard PHP and WordPress plugins with **zero Node.js in production**, you can host your app on any VPS, Docker container, or traditional LAMP/LEMP server.

## Server requirements

- **WordPress 7.1+**
- **PHP 8.2+** with the `zip` (`ZipArchive`), `openssl`, and `mbstring` extensions
- **MySQL 8.0+**, **MariaDB 10.6+**, or **SQLite** (via `sqlite-database-integration` 3.1.2+)
- HTTPS enabled (required by WordPress for Application Passwords)
- Pretty permalinks enabled (`/%postname%/`)

## Option A: Deploy with `spacepress push` (recommended)

### 1. Configure a private build store outside the web root

On nginx or any server that does not enforce `.htaccess`, point `SP_STORE_DIR` in `wp-config.php` to a writable directory **outside** your web root:

```php
define('SP_STORE_DIR', '/var/lib/spacepress-store');
```

Make sure the PHP-FPM user owns or can write to `/var/lib/spacepress-store` (`chmod 750`).

### 2. Install `spacepress.zip`

```bash
npx spacepress plugin --out spacepress.zip
```

Upload and activate `spacepress.zip` in `wp-admin` (or with `wp plugin install spacepress.zip --activate`), then authenticate and push:

```bash
npx spacepress login https://your-site.example
npx spacepress push --dry-run
npx spacepress push
```

## Option B: Deploy compiled plugins directly (Git / CI / Docker)

If your host sets `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS` or deploys immutable plugin directories via Git, rsync, or Docker images, compile the full plugin bundle locally or in CI:

```bash
npx spacepress build
```

Deploy every generated plugin from `sp/dist/wp-content/plugins/` (`spacepress-runtime`, `spacepress-identity`, `spacepress-admin`, `spacepress-app-<name>`, plus any pinned third-party plugins) into your WordPress `wp-content/plugins/` directory and activate them in order:

```bash
wp plugin activate spacepress-runtime spacepress-identity spacepress-admin spacepress-app-my-app
wp spacepress migrate
wp spacepress seed
```

## Web server & cron tips

- **Nginx routing for `public/`:** Pass unknown paths to `/index.php?$args` so SpacePress's `PublicFiles` handler serves files from `public/`, or map static files from the active app's `public/` directory directly in nginx for faster edge delivery.
- **Background jobs (`job()`):** SpacePress queues background jobs on Action Scheduler. Configure a real system cron (`* * * * * wp cron event run --due-now --path=/var/www/html`) rather than relying solely on visitor-triggered `wp-cron.php`.
- **Static export (`output: "static"`):** If your site needs no server runtime at all, run `npx spacepress export` and deploy `sp/dist/static/` to any static CDN.

fields.title: Deploy on Spacefast
fields.description: Deploy a SpacePress app to Spacefast with zero server configuration, automatic PHP compilation, and instant preview environments.

record.body:
[Spacefast](https://spacefast.com) is built to run SpacePress applications natively on WordPress 7.1+ and PHP 8.2+ without managing servers, nginx rules, or manual plugin uploads.

## Prerequisites

- A SpacePress project that passes `spacepress check` cleanly
- A [Spacefast](https://spacefast.com) account and site URL

## 1. Verify your project locally

Run a check and test build before pushing:

```bash
npx spacepress check
npx spacepress build
```

Commit your migration ledger (`sp/_generated/migrations/`) and plugin lockfile (`sp/_generated/wp-plugins.lock.json`) so every deployment upgrades your database safely and deterministically.

## 2. Sign in and preview the deployment plan

Authenticate once with your Spacefast site using WordPress Application Passwords, then inspect what the deployment will change:

```bash
npx spacepress login https://your-site.space.fast
npx spacepress push --dry-run
```

The dry run uploads your compiled runtime and app trees and prints every migration, page, and index change before making the build live.

## 3. Push to production

```bash
npx spacepress push
```

`spacepress push` atomically activates the new build, applies pending SQL migrations, seeds synced Markdown content on an empty site, and purges page caches automatically.

## 4. Sync Markdown content & verify

If your schema defines synced collections (`sync: "content/**/*.md"`), keep Git and your live Spacefast site in two-way sync:

```bash
npx spacepress sync --site https://your-site.space.fast
npx spacepress doctor --site https://your-site.space.fast --links
```

For CI pipelines, supply `SP_APP_PASSWORD="user:application-password"` as a secret environment variable instead of running `spacepress login` interactively.

fields.title: Deploy on WordPress.com
fields.description: Deploy a SpacePress app to a plugin-enabled WordPress.com site with spacepress plugin and spacepress push.

record.body:
[WordPress.com](https://wordpress.com) Business and Commerce plans run on WP Cloud with full custom plugin support, PHP 8.2+, WordPress 7.1+, SSH/WP-CLI access, and Application Passwords.

## Prerequisites

- A plugin-enabled **WordPress.com** plan (Business or Commerce) on **WordPress 7.1+** and **PHP 8.2+**
- Administrator permissions on the site

## 1. Generate and upload the SpacePress plugin

Build `spacepress.zip` locally:

```bash
npx spacepress plugin --out spacepress.zip
```

Upload and activate it via **Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin** in `wp-admin` (or via SSH/WP-CLI on your WordPress.com site):

```bash
wp plugin install spacepress.zip --activate --force
```

Activating the plugin installs the pinned runtime dependencies automatically.

## 2. Authenticate and deploy

Run `spacepress login` to authorize an Application Password in your browser, inspect the dry-run plan, and push:

```bash
npx spacepress login https://your-site.example
npx spacepress push --dry-run
npx spacepress push
```

SpacePress uploads the compiled PHP runtime and app trees, runs any new numbered SQL migrations in `sp/_generated/migrations/`, configures pretty permalinks, creates app routes, and activates the build atomically.

## 3. Sync content and verify

Sync any Markdown-backed collections and run `doctor` to verify live health and links:

```bash
npx spacepress sync --site https://your-site.example
npx spacepress doctor --site https://your-site.example --links
```

## WordPress.com hosting notes

- **Static assets under `public/`:** Like Pressable, WordPress.com runs on WP Cloud's nginx stack, which intercepts top-level `.js`, `.wasm`, and `.txt` requests before PHP and reserves `/files/*` for legacy Multisite rewrites. Place downloadable assets outside `/files/`, and copy root `.js`/`.wasm` files into `/srv/htdocs/` if your site ships custom browser bundles in `public/`.
- **Rollbacks:** Earlier builds stay in the site's build store so you can switch back to a previous release in `wp-admin` without re-uploading. Note that switching code does not revert applied SQL migrations.

fields.title: Pages, Layouts & Interactive Islands
fields.description: File-based TSX routing compiled to PHP, progressive forms, "use client" Interactivity API islands, and static export.

record.body:
## File-based routing in `sp/app/`

SpacePress compiles TSX pages and layouts in `sp/app/` directly into server-rendered PHP:

- `sp/app/layout.tsx` — shared shell, `export const template = "theme" | "blank" | "<slug>"`, `metadata`, and CSS imports.
- `sp/app/page.tsx`, `[slug]/page.tsx`, `[...path]/page.tsx`, `(group)/` — static, dynamic, catch-all, and grouped routes.
- `sp/app/not-found.tsx` and `sp/app/login.tsx` — custom 404 and custom WordPress sign-in screens.
- `export const search = { page: integer().default(1) }` — typed query string parsing.
- `export const guard = "authenticated"` — route-level authorization.

## Built-in server components (`spacepress/app`)

Use `<Link>` (Interactivity Router navigation), `<Content>` (block content via `the_content`), `<Html>` (sanitized HTML), `<Comments>`, `<Pagination>`, `<Search>`, `<SearchResults>`, `<LoginForm>`, `<TemplatePart>`, `<Live id="...">`, and `useFormState(action)` for progressive zero-JS `<form action={myAction}>` submissions.

## `"use client"` interactive islands (`spacepress/client`)

Start a component file with `"use client";`. SpacePress renders its initial HTML in PHP and compiles the interactive logic into a WordPress Interactivity API store supporting `useState`, `useEffect`, `useMount`, `useEvent`, `useRef`, `sharedState`, and live-updating `useLive(kind, query)` subscriptions.

## Static export

Set `output: "static"` in `defineConfig()` and export `staticParams()` on dynamic routes, then run `spacepress export` to emit a standalone static site to `sp/dist/static/`.

fields.title: Schema & Storage
fields.description: Collections, SQL tables, globals, WordPress built-in kinds, field builders, and migrations.

record.body:
## Choosing a storage kind

| Builder             | Storage                     | When to use                                                                                                    |
|---------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `collection()`      | WordPress custom post type  | Editorial items needing Gutenberg, drafts, revisions, staged versions, comments, URL routing, or Markdown sync |
| `table()`           | Dedicated SQL table         | Relational app records, high-volume data, compound indexes (`.index()`), strict SQL migrations                 |
| `global()`          | WordPress options singleton | Site-wide settings, navigation links, feature flags                                                            |
| `wp.posts.extend()` | Built-in WordPress `post`   | Native blog posts extended with typed meta fields and URL pattern                                              |
| `userProjection()`  | `wp_users` + `wp_usermeta`  | Typed user profiles without duplicating WordPress accounts                                                     |
| `taxonomy()`        | WordPress term tables       | Flat or hierarchical vocabularies attached via `on: [...]` or `terms()`                                        |

## Field builders

All columns are `NOT NULL` by default unless `.optional()` is chained.

- **Scalars:** `text({ multiline? })`, `integer()`, `number()`, `boolean()`, `date()`, `timestamp()`, `json<T>()`
- **Semantic:** `email()`, `url()`, `slug({ source })`, `richText()`, `select([...])` (`.many()` for multi-select)
- **Relations & Media:** `ref(kind)` (`.many()`, `.onDelete("cascade" | "restrict" | "setNull")`, `.reverse("name")`), `terms(taxonomy)`, `media({ accept })`, `file(bucket)`
- **Structured:** `group(fields)`, `repeater(fields)`, `blocks(layouts)`

## Modifiers & safe renames

Chain `.min(n)`, `.max(n)`, `.pattern(/.../)`, `.unique()`, `.default(v)`, `.defaultNow()`, `.$default(fn)`, `.$onUpdate(fn)`, `.validate((v, ctx) => ...)`, `.ui({ label, help, placeholder, width })`, and `.showIf({ ... })`.

To rename a column or SQL table without losing production data, declare `.was("oldName")` on the column or `was: "old_table"` on `table()`. SpacePress emits a safe rename migration against `sp/_generated/migrations/snapshot.json`.

fields.title: Installation & Setup
fields.description: Requirements, creating a new app, and starting the local WordPress development environment.

record.body:
## Requirements

- **Node.js 22 or newer** and npm
- No Docker and no Rust toolchain required — the `spacepress` npm package downloads a prebuilt native compiler binary automatically.

## Create a new application

```bash
npm create spacepress@0.3.0 my-app
cd my-app
npm run dev
```

`create-spacepress` creates a complete starter project with:

- `spacepress.config.ts` defining a synced `notes` collection and `site` global
- `sp/app/` with a layout, home page, dynamic `/notes/[slug]` page, and a progressive `<form action={greet}>`
- `content/notes/` sample Markdown content
- `AGENTS.md`, `.mcp.json`, and coding-agent skills generated via `spacepress init`

## Running locally

`npm run dev` invokes `spacepress dev`, which compiles your TypeScript, boots a local WordPress + SQLite server, activates the compiled plugins, and rebuilds automatically on file changes.

- Open the printed site URL to view your rendered TSX pages.
- Open `/wp-admin/new/` to explore SpacePress Admin (or `/wp-admin/` for classic wp-admin).
- Stop the dev server without deleting local data via `npm run stop` (`spacepress dev stop`).

## Adding modules

Add first-party modules as source files you own at any time:

```bash
npx spacepress add shop           # WooCommerce storefront & catalog
npx spacepress add db             # SQL table starter
npx spacepress add api-reference  # /api documentation pages from OpenAPI
```

fields.title: Project Structure
fields.description: Layout of a SpacePress repository, authored files vs generated artifacts.

record.body:
## Directory layout

```text
my-app/
├── spacepress.config.ts   # Entry point: defineConfig() + re-exports
├── tsconfig.json          # Maps "spacepress", "spacepress/*", "spacepress:db"
├── sp/
│   ├── schema.ts          # Collections, SQL tables, globals, taxonomies, stores
│   ├── server.ts          # Actions, background jobs, mail helpers
│   ├── app/               # File-based TSX pages, layouts, and route.ts handlers
│   ├── components/        # Server and "use client" components
│   ├── wp-hooks/          # Typed WordPress core action & filter handlers
│   ├── _generated/        # db.d.ts, routes.d.ts, openapi.json, client/, migrations/
│   └── dist/wp-content/   # Compiled WordPress plugins ready to deploy
├── content/               # Markdown/JSON content synced with WordPress
├── emails/                # React Email (.tsx) templates
└── public/                # Static assets served from site root
```

## What to commit to Git

Commit everything you author (`spacepress.config.ts`, `sp/schema.ts`, `sp/app/`, `content/`, `emails/`, `public/`) **plus** these compiler lock/ledger files:

- `sp/_generated/migrations/` (`snapshot.json` and numbered `*.sql` files) — tracks schema history for safe incremental deploys.
- `sp/_generated/wp-plugins.lock.json` — locks WordPress plugin versions and SHA-256 checksums.
- `sp/_generated/plugins.lock.json` — locks capability grants for `use` plugin packages.
- `sp/_generated/abilities.json` & `sp/_generated/runtime-schema.json` — when using pulled WordPress Abilities or runtime schema versions.

`sp/dist/` is a build artifact and is typically git-ignored.

fields.title: Astro & Generated Typed Clients
fields.description: Connect external React, Next.js, Vite, or Astro frontends to a SpacePress backend.

record.body:
## Generated TypeScript client & React hooks

Every build emits a typed client to `sp/_generated/client/`:

- `index.ts` — `createClient({ baseUrl })` for CRUD queries, pagination, live subscriptions, and typed server actions.
- `react.ts` — `createHooks(React)` returning `useQuery()` and `useMutation()` (with `optimistic` updates and rollback) for React 18+ or Preact without bundling React into SpacePress.

## `@spacepress/astro`

For Astro 7+ sites, install `@spacepress/astro`:

- `spLoader(kind, opts)` — build-time Astro Content Layer loader with relation and media expansion.
- `spLiveLoader(kind, opts)` — live on-demand loader returning `cacheHint.tags` (`<kind>`, `<kind>:<id>`).
- `spWebhook(opts)` — Astro API route handler verifying `SpacePress-Signature` HMAC headers and invalidating cache tags automatically.

Set `frontend: "https://your-astro-site.com"` in `defineConfig()` so WordPress permalinks, previews, and feeds point to your Astro deployment.

fields.title: Two-Way Markdown & Git Sync
fields.description: Synchronize Markdown/JSON files in Git with WordPress collections and taxonomies.

record.body:
## Configuring sync

Add a `sync` glob to any `collection()`, `wp.posts.extend()`, `taxonomy()`, `product()`, or `table()`:

```ts
export const docs = collection({
  title: text(),
  slug: slug({ source: "title" }),
  content: richText().optional(),
}, {
  hierarchical: true,
  url: "/docs/:path",
  sync: "content/docs/**/*.md",
});
```

A `**` folder pattern maps subdirectories into parent/child hierarchy (`index.md` represents the folder item). Every synced record receives an immutable `uid` so renames and slug changes stay linked.

## Running sync & CI workflows

- Run `spacepress sync` to perform a 3-way merge between local Markdown files and WordPress. Front matter is validated against your TypeScript schema before writing.
- Run `spacepress init --github` to scaffold GitHub Actions for automated content sync.
- Configure `spacepress git-dispatch` so edits saved inside WordPress Admin trigger a repository dispatch event automatically.
- Enable `seed: true` in `defineConfig()` to populate synced records when a fresh deployment activates the plugin without overwriting existing editorial changes.

fields.title: CLI & Deployment
fields.description: Build, check, export, push, doctor, plugin packaging, and production hosting options.

record.body:
## Core build & deploy commands

- `spacepress dev` / `dev stop` / `dev status` — manage the local WordPress + SQLite site.
- `spacepress check [--json] [--frozen]` — compile and report diagnostics without writing output.
- `spacepress build` — emit WordPress plugins into `sp/dist/wp-content/plugins/`, migrations, types, client, and OpenAPI.
- `spacepress export [--site <url>]` — prebuild `sp/app/` into `sp/dist/static/` (`output: "static"`).
- `spacepress plugin` — package an uploadable `spacepress.zip` plugin for `wp-admin`.
- `spacepress login <site-url>` & `spacepress push` — authenticate via WordPress Application Passwords and deploy directly to a remote WordPress site.
- `spacepress doctor [--links]` — verify build integrity, live site plugins, and crawl internal links/anchors.

## Site operations (WP-CLI bridge)

Target local dev (default) or any remote site (`--site <dir | workspace | @alias>`):

- `spacepress wp <args...>` — run any WP-CLI command.
- `spacepress migrate`, `seed`, `jobs`, `staged`, `publish-due`, `identity`, `find`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `action`, `abilities`, `run`.

## Hosting & deployment guides

SpacePress runs anywhere WordPress 7.1+ and PHP 8.2+ run:

- **[Deploy on Spacefast](/docs/operations/deploy-spacefast)**
- **[Deploy on Pressable](/docs/operations/deploy-pressable)**
- **[Deploy on WordPress.com](/docs/operations/deploy-wordpress-com)**
- **[Deploy on Self-hosted WordPress](/docs/operations/deploy-self-hosted)**

## Sealed mode & plugin lockfile

Declare third-party WordPress plugins in `defineConfig({ plugins: { ... }, sealed: true })`. Exact versions and SHA-256 checksums are locked in `sp/_generated/wp-plugins.lock.json`, and sealed mode refuses activation of undeclared plugins.

fields.title: MCP & AI Agents
fields.description: Project MCP server, AGENTS.md scaffolding, WordPress Abilities API, and runtime schema versions.

record.body:
## Coding agent setup

Run `spacepress init` in any project to write `AGENTS.md`, `.mcp.json`, and agent skills tailored to your schema and config. Run `spacepress init --check` in CI to ensure they stay up to date.

## Stdio MCP server

`spacepress mcp` launches a local MCP server on stdio exposing:

- Embedded documentation compiled into the exact binary version you are running
- Live project schema, routes, and compiler diagnostics

## WordPress Abilities API

Every collection, global, action, and job is registered as a WordPress Ability by default (`agents: false` opts out). Annotate actions with `readonly: true` or `destructive: true` to guide agent safety checks.

To invoke abilities provided by WordPress core or installed plugins with full TypeScript types:

```bash
npx spacepress abilities pull --site https://example.com
```

Then call `abilities.call("ability/name", input)` from `"php/wordpress"` inside any action, hook, or route.

fields.title: Deploy on Pressable
fields.description: Deploy a SpacePress app to Pressable (WP Cloud) using the SpacePress plugin, Application Passwords, and spacepress push.

record.body:
[Pressable](https://pressable.com) runs managed WordPress on WP Cloud with PHP 8.2+, WordPress 7.1+, `ZipArchive`, WP-CLI over SSH, and Application Passwords enabled over HTTPS. `spacepress.dev` itself runs on Pressable.

## Prerequisites

- A Pressable site running **WordPress 7.1+** and **PHP 8.2+**
- Administrator access in `wp-admin` (or SSH/WP-CLI access)

## 1. Package and install the SpacePress plugin

Generate the uploadable host plugin (`spacepress.zip`):

```bash
npx spacepress plugin --out spacepress.zip
```

Install and activate `spacepress.zip` in **wp-admin → Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin**, or over SSH with WP-CLI:

```bash
wp plugin install spacepress.zip --activate --force
```

Activating the plugin automatically installs and activates its pinned platform dependencies (`action-scheduler`, `secure-custom-fields`, `two-factor`, `mcp-adapter`).

## 2. Sign in and push your build

Authenticate against your Pressable site and preview the deployment plan:

```bash
npx spacepress login https://your-site.example
npx spacepress push --dry-run
```

When the plan looks right, make it live:

```bash
npx spacepress push
```

In CI or non-interactive scripts, create a WordPress Application Password (`wp user application-password create <user> deploy --porcelain`) and pass `SP_APP_PASSWORD="<user>:<password>"`.

## 3. Sync Markdown content

If you use `sync: "content/**/*.md"`, push or pull Markdown edits after deploying:

```bash
npx spacepress sync --site https://your-site.example
```

## Pressable / WP Cloud hosting notes

- **Build store location:** On Pressable, PHP-FPM runs inside `/srv/htdocs` and cannot write outside it, so SpacePress automatically creates a randomized build store directory (`wp-content/spacepress-store-<random-hex>`). Keep that path private and never link to it publicly.
- **Root static files (`.js`, `.wasm`, `.txt`):** Pressable's nginx serves top-level static file extensions directly from `/srv/htdocs/` before reaching PHP. If your app ships custom scripts or WebAssembly assets under `public/` (like `public/site.js` or `public/compiler.wasm`), copy them into `/srv/htdocs/` during release so nginx serves them directly from the edge CDN.
- **Avoid `/files/` for public assets:** WP Cloud reserves `/files/*` for legacy WordPress Multisite rewrites. Place downloadable assets in another path (for example, `public/downloads/` or `public/playground-plugins/`).

fields.title: Deploy on Self-hosted WordPress
fields.description: Run SpacePress on your own VPS, Docker stack, or any LAMP/LEMP host with zero lock-in — via spacepress push or standalone plugins.

record.body:
Because SpacePress compiles into standard PHP and WordPress plugins with **zero Node.js in production**, you can host your app on any VPS, Docker container, or traditional LAMP/LEMP server.

## Server requirements

- **WordPress 7.1+**
- **PHP 8.2+** with the `zip` (`ZipArchive`), `openssl`, and `mbstring` extensions
- **MySQL 8.0+**, **MariaDB 10.6+**, or **SQLite** (via `sqlite-database-integration` 3.1.2+)
- HTTPS enabled (required by WordPress for Application Passwords)
- Pretty permalinks enabled (`/%postname%/`)

## Option A: Deploy with `spacepress push` (recommended)

### 1. Configure a private build store outside the web root

On nginx or any server that does not enforce `.htaccess`, point `SP_STORE_DIR` in `wp-config.php` to a writable directory **outside** your web root:

```php
<?php
define('SP_STORE_DIR', '/var/lib/spacepress-store');
```

Make sure the PHP-FPM user owns or can write to `/var/lib/spacepress-store` (`chmod 750`).

### 2. Install `spacepress.zip`

```bash
npx spacepress plugin --out spacepress.zip
```

Upload and activate `spacepress.zip` in `wp-admin` (or with `wp plugin install spacepress.zip --activate`), then authenticate and push:

```bash
npx spacepress login https://your-site.example
npx spacepress push --dry-run
npx spacepress push
```

## Option B: Deploy compiled plugins directly (Git / CI / Docker)

If your host sets `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS` or deploys immutable plugin directories via Git, rsync, or Docker images, compile the full plugin bundle locally or in CI:

```bash
npx spacepress build
```

Deploy every generated plugin from `sp/dist/wp-content/plugins/` (`spacepress-runtime`, `spacepress-identity`, `spacepress-admin`, `spacepress-app-<name>`, plus any pinned third-party plugins) into your WordPress `wp-content/plugins/` directory and activate them in order:

```bash
wp plugin activate spacepress-runtime spacepress-identity spacepress-admin spacepress-app-my-app
wp spacepress migrate
wp spacepress seed
```

## Web server & cron tips

- **Nginx routing for `public/`:** Pass unknown paths to `/index.php?$args` so SpacePress's `PublicFiles` handler serves files from `public/`, or map static files from the active app's `public/` directory directly in nginx for faster edge delivery.
- **Background jobs (`job()`):** SpacePress queues background jobs on Action Scheduler. Configure a real system cron (`* * * * * wp cron event run --due-now --path=/var/www/html`) rather than relying solely on visitor-triggered `wp-cron.php`.
- **Static export (`output: "static"`):** If your site needs no server runtime at all, run `npx spacepress export` and deploy `sp/dist/static/` to any static CDN.

fields.title: Deploy on Spacefast
fields.description: Deploy a SpacePress app to Spacefast with zero server configuration, automatic PHP compilation, and instant preview environments.

record.body:
[Spacefast](https://spacefast.com) is built to run SpacePress applications natively on WordPress 7.1+ and PHP 8.2+ without managing servers, nginx rules, or manual plugin uploads.

## Prerequisites

- A SpacePress project that passes `spacepress check` cleanly
- A [Spacefast](https://spacefast.com) account and site URL

## 1. Verify your project locally

Run a check and test build before pushing:

```bash
npx spacepress check
npx spacepress build
```

Commit your migration ledger (`sp/_generated/migrations/`) and plugin lockfile (`sp/_generated/wp-plugins.lock.json`) so every deployment upgrades your database safely and deterministically.

## 2. Sign in and preview the deployment plan

Authenticate once with your Spacefast site using WordPress Application Passwords, then inspect what the deployment will change:

```bash
npx spacepress login https://your-site.space.fast
npx spacepress push --dry-run
```

The dry run uploads your compiled runtime and app trees and prints every migration, page, and index change before making the build live.

## 3. Push to production

```bash
npx spacepress push
```

`spacepress push` atomically activates the new build, applies pending SQL migrations, seeds synced Markdown content on an empty site, and purges page caches automatically.

## 4. Sync Markdown content & verify

If your schema defines synced collections (`sync: "content/**/*.md"`), keep Git and your live Spacefast site in two-way sync:

```bash
npx spacepress sync --site https://your-site.space.fast
npx spacepress doctor --site https://your-site.space.fast --links
```

For CI pipelines, supply `SP_APP_PASSWORD="user:application-password"` as a secret environment variable instead of running `spacepress login` interactively.


Activating the plugin installs the pinned runtime dependencies automatically.

## 2. Authenticate and deploy

```bash
npx spacepress login https://your-site.example
npx spacepress push --dry-run
npx spacepress push
```

SpacePress uploads the compiled PHP runtime and app trees, runs any new numbered SQL migrations in `sp/_generated/migrations/`, configures pretty permalinks, creates app routes, and activates the build atomically.

## 3. Sync content and verify

Sync any Markdown-backed collections and run `doctor` to verify live health and links:

```bash
npx spacepress sync --site https://your-site.example
npx spacepress doctor --site https://your-site.example --links
```

## WordPress.com hosting notes

Place downloadable assets outside `/files/`, and copy root `.js`/`.wasm` files into `/srv/htdocs/` if your site ships custom browser bundles in `public/`.
- **Rollbacks:** Earlier builds stay in the site's build store so you can switch back to a previous release in `wp-admin` without re-uploading. Note that switching code does not revert applied SQL migrations.

fields.title: Introducing SpacePress: TypeScript That Compiles Directly to WordPress
fields.excerpt: Write schemas, SQL tables, access rules, server actions, background jobs, and TSX pages in TypeScript — compiled with Rust into native PHP and WordPress plugins with zero Node.js in production.

record.body:
Today we are introducing **SpacePress** (`spacepress.dev`) — a full-stack TypeScript framework whose Rust and OXC compiler turns your application directly into native PHP, numbered SQL migrations, OpenAPI 3.1, a typed client, and standard WordPress plugins.

## Why compile TypeScript to WordPress?

Teams building content-heavy products, editorial sites, and storefronts face an awkward split: either adopt a modern TypeScript stack and rebuild editorial workflows, media libraries, permissions, comments, and commerce from scratch — or adopt WordPress and give up end-to-end type safety, clean migrations, and modern component authoring.

SpacePress bridges both worlds without running a Node.js server in production:

- **One TypeScript schema, two storage engines:** Use `collection()` for WordPress posts (with Gutenberg, drafts, revisions, staged versions, and comments) right alongside `table()` for relational SQL tables with automatic migrations and compound indexes.
- **Native PHP compilation:** Declarative access rules, field validation, transactional hooks, `action()` RPC endpoints, Action Scheduler `job()` queues, custom `route.ts` handlers, and file-based TSX pages all compile directly to PHP.
- **Progressive interactivity:** Forms bound to server actions work without JavaScript, while `"use client"` components compile to WordPress Interactivity API stores with `useState` and live-updating `useLive()`.
- **Ecosystem included:** Native WooCommerce store & optimistic cart hooks, React Email transactional templates, two-way Markdown & Git sync, modern SpacePress Admin (`/wp-admin/new/`), `@spacepress/blocks` for Gutenberg in TSX, `@spacepress/astro` for external frontends, and a built-in MCP server for AI coding agents.

## Built with SpacePress itself

Everything you are reading on **spacepress.dev** is itself a real SpacePress application:

- This blog post is synced from `www/content/posts/introducing-spacepress.md` via `wp.posts.extend()` and rendered through `sp/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` with WordPress's native `<Comments>` component.
- The `/docs` section is synced from `www/content/docs/**/*.md` into a hierarchical `docs` collection rendered with `nav()`, `pager()`, and `headings()`.
- The `/examples` directory lives in a custom SQL `table()` whose GitHub star counts refresh asynchronously on Action Scheduler via the `refreshStars` job.
- Saved links in the `/play` browser playground are stored in the `shares` SQL table via the `share` server action, while the live compiler sandboxes across `/`, `/quick-start`, `/handbook`, and `/play` run our real Rust compiler compiled to WebAssembly (`compiler.wasm`).

## Try it now

Head to the [Quick Start](/quick-start) to launch a local WordPress site in under three minutes, explore the [Interactive Handbook](/handbook) with live compiler sandboxes in every section, or jump straight into the [Playground](/play) right in your browser.
